title: The Border of the Free Port
premise: Felix Underhill has spent a decade making dirty money look clean on paper so quietly that her own agency barely admits she exists. When an anonymous voiceprint—her own, aged ten years—unlocks a dead man's server in a Baltic free port, she finds a ledger implicating the very officials who fund her unit. The trail leads to Marek Voss, a defector hiding inside the port's extraterritorial zone, who claims the ledger is bait designed to flush out anyone still honest. Felix extracts Voss anyway, discovers he engineered the voiceprint to recruit her, and in the end she chooses neither silence nor the law: she detonates the ledger publicly, burns her own invisibility, and walks out of the free port a person with a name, hunted but finally accountable.
about_author: Sable Montrose is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent nine years inside the plumbing of offshore finance before leaving to write. They live near a port city they refuse to name, and their debut novel draws on the strange legal geography of free ports and the people who vanish into them.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In a gray London office, Felix launders a corrupt minister's reputation through paperwork so elegant no one will ever notice. Her supervisor praises her precisely because her name appears nowhere. Emotional beat: the hollow comfort of being unattributable.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A routine archive migration pings her: a server in the Baltische Freihafen accepts a voiceprint that matches her own voice, aged. She plays it forty times, telling no one. Emotional beat: vertigo—someone has been rehearsing her future.

chapters.title: Unattributed
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She pulls her own personnel file and finds her title redacted even to herself. Her only colleague, Denny Okafor, notices her distraction and covers for her, badly. Emotional beat: the first crack in her chosen anonymity.

chapters.title: The Free Port
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Flashback-laced travel: Felix arrives in the Baltic free port, a zone where customs, courts, and clocks all politely stop working. She registers under a false name and immediately feels watched. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Server
chapters.summary: POV Felix. In a bonded warehouse, she speaks the aged phrase aloud and the dead auditor Ilmars Kalns' server opens: a ledger naming funders of her own unit, including her director, Ruth Calloway. Emotional beat: betrayal as a physical blow.

chapters.title: The Man in Bond 7
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Defector Marek Voss watches Felix on a smuggled camera feed and reports to an unknown handler that 'she took the bait—maybe.' His loyalties are deliberately unclear. Emotional beat: the hunter revealed as a lure.

chapters.title: Ledger of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The ledger's entries are dated in the future. Either it's fabricated, or someone is planning corruption before committing it. She copies it three ways and destroys the original. Emotional beat: dread of a machine that writes its own alibis.

chapters.title: Calloway Calls
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Back home, Director Ruth Calloway learns Felix used leave she never approved. She orders a quiet flag on Felix's passport—not an arrest, an erasure. Emotional beat: corruption as calm administration.

chapters.title: Someone Following, Someone Waiting
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Tailed through the port's duty-free corridors, Felix loses her shadow in a champagne warehouse and is found instead by Marek, who knows her real name. Emotional beat: the trap closing, and curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: Voss's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek claims Kalns was his partner and the future-dated ledger is real: a privatized justice system being pre-purchased. He offers Felix the extraction route in exchange for her testimony. Emotional beat: a bargain that feels like a script someone else wrote.

chapters.title: What the Voiceprint Knew
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She realizes the voiceprint was synthesized from her own archived testimony—recorded by her own agency, meaning the trap was set from inside. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of being betrayed with your own voice.

chapters.title: Denny's Question
chapters.summary: POV Denny. In London, Denny covers Felix's absence and starts asking dangerous questions of his own. Calloway offers him Felix's job. He neither accepts nor refuses. Emotional beat: loyalty under quiet purchase.

chapters.title: The Extraction
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix and Marek move at shift-change through the port's sealed zone, using a refrigerated container and a bribed gate clerk. It works until it doesn't: the gate clerk's radio crackles with her description. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the discovery she trusts Marek against her judgment.

chapters.title: Interlude at Sea
chapters.summary: POV Marek. On a fishing trawler, Marek tells Felix a version of his past that is too polished. She catches one detail that contradicts Kalns' files and says nothing. Emotional beat: intimacy built on mutual concealment.

chapters.title: The Port Closes
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Calloway invokes an emergency clause and seals the free port's records with foreign partners—erasing the ledger's corroborating documents. Felix's extraction window shrinks to hours. Emotional beat: power as paperwork, violence as a signature.

chapters.title: Return to Bond 7
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Forced back inside the port, Felix finds Kalns' second server and learns the truth: Marek wrote the future-dated ledger himself, as bait for Calloway's network—and needed someone unattributable to carry it out. Emotional beat: rage at being chosen for her invisibility.

chapters.title: The Confrontation in the Vault
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek admits it: Kalns is alive, hidden, and the ledger's future dates are his own planned testimony. He argues the only justice left is a public detonation. Calloway's men breach the vault. Emotional beat: the argument Felix can't refute and can't forgive.

chapters.title: What Calloway Wants
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Calloway corners Felix alone and offers her everything: attribution, promotion, a clean ledger of her own—if she surrenders the files and lets Marek vanish. Emotional beat: temptation voiced in perfectly reasonable tones.

chapters.title: The Choice of Names
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix refuses, signs her real name to an affidavit, and triggers the ledger's dead-man release to two hundred journalists simultaneously. Alarms rise through the port. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into authorship.

chapters.title: Detonation
chapters.summary: POV Felix and Marek, alternating. The publication hits as Calloway's team storms the warehouse. Denny, tipped by Felix, stalls the London end just long enough. Kalns surfaces on camera, alive, corroborating everything. Emotional beat: chaos as the sound of a locked system opening.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Attributed
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Weeks later: inquiries open, Calloway arrested mid-resignation, Marek granted a fragile asylum that may be another trap. Felix testifies under her own name and loses her anonymity permanently. Emotional beat: grief for the invisible life, and no regret.

chapters.title: The Border of the Free Port
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Felix returns to the port's edge as a witness, not a ghost, and watches the zone's gates open to ordinary customs for the first time in decades. A voiceprint prompt asks her to identify herself; she says her name aloud. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, ending at the border of the accountable self.
